name: maybe_Ui_Widget_DeletingDtorA
summary: Stores the vtable word handed in by the caller at self+0x00, runs the shared scene-node/widget base destructor and then deletes the object through its own vtable. One of the many generated deleting-destructor thunks of the Ui widget hierarchy.
evidence: Body: str r1,[r0]; bl 0x1D8C2C (inner entry of 0x1D8BD4 maybe_Field_DestroyNode = base destructor that installs vtable 0x0075A3F4 and unlinks the node lists); b 0x10F6CC (delete object through vtable, used by every deleting dtor in this range). No callers: reached only through a vtable.

name: maybe_Container_InlineVector_PushRecord
signature: void maybe_Container_InlineVector_PushRecord(InlineVector* self, const TextSlotSource* src, int len, void* unused, u8 flag)
summary: Appends one 44-byte record (two short wide strings plus a flag byte) to a vector that keeps its elements inline: begin/end/capacity at +4/+8/+0xC, inline buffer at +0x14. Builds the strings from src+0 and src+0x3C with wcslen/wcsncpy (SSO, 6 chars max) and reallocates through the object's own allocator when end == capacity.
evidence: Entry guard compares end-begin with 0x580 and checks begin == self+0x14 (inline storage); element size 0x2C recovered from the growth code (magic 0x2E8BA2E9 = /0x2C); callees std_wcsncpy, 0x00100B74 (wcslen) and std_memcpy; the source strings are at arg2 and arg2+0x3C and the tail byte comes from the 5th stack argument.

name: maybe_Container_HashBucket_FindByType
summary: Looks a key up in the global bucket table at 0x007B80C0: index = key & (hashMask>>10), bucket must carry the same key>>11, then each chained object is asked for its type tag through vtbl[0] and compared with the static descriptor 0x007C5078; follows +0xC while it does not match. Returns the matching object or NULL.
evidence: Body reads g_007B80C0 + (idx<<3), compares the second bucket word with r0>>11, then calls (*(*obj))() and compares against the address of the bss descriptor 0x007C5078; chain walk through [obj+0xC]. Same bucket table and same key>>11 trick as 0x00245BC0 (maybe_Ui_Toggle_FreeHandle), so the table is the engine's global handle registry; the 'find by type' reading is inferred from the type-tag compare.

name: maybe_Container_InlineSlot_PopFront
summary: Removes the first element of a small inline slot container: returns the old key from +4, logs the new head through the engine trace formatter, slides the 0x20-byte payload from +0xC down to +4 with memmove and clears the counter at +0x24.
evidence: Body: returns [self+4]; if the global trace object 0x007AC834 is set it calls 0x707C1C (varargs formatter) with the inline format at 0x2C6BF4 and self+8; then 0x11CD00 (= memmove) copies 0x20 bytes from self+0xC to self+4; self+0x24 = 0. Appears in the pointer table at 0x0078059C next to 0x1A5EE0 (list-empty test), so it is a container operation, not a game action.

name: maybe_Ui_JackpotScreen_SetNextStepUpdateReels
summary: Advances the jackpot screen one step by copying table entry 7 of the screen's step table (0x0072AA0C, whose entry 7 is maybe_Ui_JackpotScreen_UpdateReels) into the current-step pair at self+0x50, unless the reel animation attached through self+0x44 is still running.
evidence: Loads 0x0072AA0C and stores ldrd [table+0x38] (= entry 7 = 0x002C7EEC maybe_Ui_JackpotScreen_UpdateReels, 0) into self+0x50 (the {func,arg} step pair used by every step function in this table). Guard: 0x64E948(self->f_44+0x30AC) returns 1 while the anim is still running (it tests a float at +0x24 against a constant). This function is itself entry 51 of the same table (maybe_Ui_IconList_UpdateState neighbour).

name: maybe_Ui_JackpotScreen_HandleCursorMove
summary: Input block of the icon-list/jackpot screen: on left/right it advances the highlighted column, on up/down it moves the slider value, plays cursor SEs 3749/3750 (0x0EA5/0x0EA6) when the value actually changes, refreshes the icon list, then pushes the new cursor and value into the reel window and the status panel before running the next screen callback.
evidence: Not a real entry point: 0x2C8EA2 is 2 bytes into an ARM instruction of FUN_002C8D22, the rest (0x2C8EC0-0x2C90CC) is a coherent block reachable only by branches. Contents: tst r5,#0x10 / #0x280 / ldrb [r4,#0x3C]&4, Sound_PlaySeById(0xEA5/0xEA6), Ui_IconList_RefreshIcons(0x2C7D54), 0x30DC18/0x30D674 on self+0x44 (the reel window), 0x405D90/0x405E00 (seven-digit number formatting into the panel at +0x11C), 0x4DC4F0, then Ui_Screen_InvokeNextCallback.

name: maybe_Container_ReleaseRefHandleArrays
summary: Destructor of a container that owns six dynamic arrays of reference-counted handles (count/pointer pairs at +0x34/0x38, +0x3C/0x40, +0x44/0x48, +0x4C/0x50 for 0x14-byte records, +0x24/0x28, plus the small table at +0x28). For every handle it decrements the object's refcount at obj+4 and calls vtable[2] when it reaches zero, then runs the container's own vtable destructor and frees the block with its computed byte size.
evidence: Six repetitions of the same refcount-release sequence: tst handle,#0x8000000, ldr ptr,[handle+4], ldr ref,[ptr+4], subs/str, blx [vtable+8] on zero - the engine's reference-counted handle convention (same as 0x002CC598 / 0x002CC614 in this batch). Tail computes (counts*8 + records*0x14 + 0x60) and tail-calls 0x147AEC (sized free through the heap vtable at 0x007AEABC).

name: maybe_Container_RefPair_DeletingDtor
summary: Deleting destructor for an object holding two reference-counted handles: stores the new tag word at +0, releases the handles at +0x14 and +0xC (refcount decrement, vtable[2] on zero) and then destroys/frees the object through 0x1E912C.
evidence: Two copies of the release sequence on self+0x14 and self+0xC, then sub r0,r4,#0xC (back to the object base) and b 0x1E912C, which installs vtable 0x0075A728 and resets the child pointer at +8 - i.e. a base destructor/delete. Tag stored at +0 is a refcounted handle word test target (0x8000000 flag).

name: maybe_Container_NotifyAllAndRegister
summary: One-shot initialiser guarded by bit 31 of self+4: it sets the flag, forwards the given value to every element of the array at self+0x28 (count at +0x2C), then links itself into the listener list of the object at self+0x14 (+0x48) and finally registers into that object with 0x245C1C.
evidence: Guard: tst [r0+4],#0x80000000 / bne return, then orr 0x80000000 and store => 'already done' bit. Loop over [self+0x28] with stride 8 calls 0x245C80 (0x245BC0+0xC0). Then 0x245C40(self->f_14+0x48, self) is an intrusive-list unlink/relink, and the tail call 0x245C1C(value, self) inserts into a list at +0xC/+0x10.

name: maybe_Ui_Object_DeleteDtor48
summary: Deleting destructor of a 0x48-byte object: calls the object's own first virtual function (the class destructor chain) and frees the 0x48-byte block through 0x147AEC.
evidence: Body: (*(*self))(self); then mov r1,#0x48 and tail-call 0x147AEC (sized free). Entered from the pointer table at 0x0076029C; 0x2CC6B0 right after it is a separate 0x28-byte function (it uses Sq_Stack_Resize on self+0x28), so only the first 0x28 bytes belong to this function.

name: maybe_Fs_FormatDataPath
signature: int maybe_Fs_FormatDataPath(char* dst, int dstSize, const char* root, int index, ...)
summary: Formats a resource path of the form "<root>/Data<index>" into the caller's buffer. Used by the model/asset loader when it has to name the per-variant sub-file ('Data0', 'Data1', ...) below a model directory.

Arguments: r0=dst(arg2), r1=size(arg3), r2=inline format "%s/Data%d" at 0x002CC828, r3=pointer to the string "data:" at 0x0072D780, stack=arg4. name: maybe_Ui_PageList_StepCounterDown

evidence: Calls 0x6221D0(self+0x54, 0). 0x6221D0 splits a value into quotient/remainder (magic 0x66666667 = /10 for the per-digit display), stores the quotient at +0x10 and formats both halves with the UTF-16 "%d" literal at 0x006221C8 into the two text widgets at +4/+8. Then (*vtable)[0x6C](self, self->f_64) dispatches to the owner. Lives in the same vtable as Ui_RowListWindow_LoadPage and maybe_Ui_PageList_ShowPage, so it is a pager operation; 'counter' rather than 'page' because two numbers are refreshed.

name: maybe_Ui_PageList_StepCounterUp

name: maybe_Ui_Widget_RelocateRecordPointerA
signature: void maybe_Ui_Widget_RelocateRecordPointerA(UiWidget* self, void* record, void* loader)
summary: Layout-load fix-up: marks the loader's 'relocating' field (+0x60C) with the address of the pointer being patched, converts the stored offset through the widget's relocation table (self+0xA8) and writes the resolved pointer back into the record, then clears the marker.

Second identical copy at 0x002D00AC. Both are vtable rows of the Ui widget/layout object at 0x00760498/0x0076049C next to maybe_Ui_Widget_ApplyScreenTransform.

name: maybe_Ui_SmithMenu_PlayOutcomeText

name: maybe_Anim_StateDispatch_ThunkA
signature: void maybe_Anim_StateDispatch_ThunkA(void* self, int group, int slot)
summary: One-instruction thunk that forwards all three arguments unchanged to 0x006C8108, the 3x4 animation/event dispatcher (group at [self+4] 0..2, slot 0..3). Used as a vtable slot so that a class can expose the dispatcher without its own code.
evidence: push {r4,lr}; bl 0x006C8108; pop {r4,pc} with r0/r1/r2 untouched. 0x006C8108 selects handler [ (self->f_4)*3 + slot ] from a 16-byte-stride table at self+0x30+slot*8 and tail-calls it; r4 is pushed but unused, the classic signature of a generated vtable thunk.

name: maybe_Anim_StateDispatch_ThunkB
signature: void maybe_Anim_StateDispatch_ThunkB(void* self, int group, int slot)
summary: Second generated thunk for the same 0x006C8108 animation/event dispatcher (identical to 0x002D1588); the code at 0x002D1810 that follows it is a separate state-normalisation helper (7/5->6, 3/1->2) and not part of this function.

name: maybe_Anim_Clip_UpdateTimerAndDispatch

evidence: Shape is identical to 0x006C80BC (the engine's clip timer): (*(*[r4]))(...) via vtbl[0x10] = is-finished test, then [r4+8] += s16, [r4+0xC] += 1, then bl 0x006C8108 with (self+0x3C, 1, 0). Vtable row 0x00760590 in the Anim_Clip/ClipSet table that also holds Anim_ClipSet_Refresh.

name: maybe_Ui_LayoutAnim_SwitchCaseBlock

name: maybe_Ui_Widget_DelegateTrampolines
summary: A block of eight tiny vtable trampolines (0x2D5E28..0x2D5EB4) that all load a 64-bit value from their object and forward it either to the callback binder 0x7230BC with one of three fixed callbacks (0x00154BE8 / 0x00150FB8 / 0x001492BC) or to the state setter 0x722EDC with a constant 0..5. Ghidra merged them into one entry that begins with a jump table.
evidence: Disassembly starts with 'ldrlo pc,[pc,r1,lsl#2]' (a jump table) followed by 8 stubs: ldrd r0,r1,[r0]; bl 0x7230BC with r2 = 0x154BE8/0x150FB8/0x1492BC, then six stubs ldrd; bl 0x722EDC with r2 = 0..5. 0x7230BC is an entry inside FUN_00722FD4 and 0x722EDC inside FUN_00722A50, both part of the Gfx/Ui render command module.

name: maybe_Ui_List_GetPendingCode
summary: Returns 14 when the signed byte flag at self+0x1C is set, otherwise -1; a small status/result selector used by the caller to decide between 'has pending work' and 'nothing to do'.
evidence: Body: ldrsb r0,[r0,#0x1C]; if (r0) r0 = 0xE else r0 = -1. No callers and no data references, so only the shape is known; the 0xE/-1 pair looks like a request id / error code.

evidence: First half calls (*(self->f_14))->vtbl[0x14](self+0x14) to fetch the value; the tail at 0x002D9A04 writes [self+0x120+4]=float const, +8=0, +9=0xA, +1=1. Vtable row 0x00780900 directly next to maybe_Ui_Widget_StartSubTween / maybe_Ui_Widget_StopSubTween and 0x002D9A2C.

name: maybe_Ui_Widget_BeginSubTweenOut
summary: Starts the opposite sub-tween: marks the target object (self->f_14->vtbl[0x14] result) with byte +0x6D = 1, sets the running flag at self+0x120 and clears the 'reverse' flag.
evidence: Same prologue as 0x002D99DC, but writes strb r2=1,[r1+0x6D], strb [r0]=1, strb [r0+1]=0. The code at 0x002D9A6C that follows is the per-frame updater of the same block (it computes 1 - progress/duration, clamps it, stores the float at target+0x74 and clears the flags when done); listed separately here only because the batch range covers it.
